'''Alexander Canterell Johnson''' (born February 8, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played two seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. Johnson played [[college basketball]] for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] before being selected 45th overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. In the [[NBA]], he played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and [[Miami Heat]].

==Early life and college==
Johnson attended [[Dougherty Comprehensive High School]] in [[Albany, Georgia]] and played collegiately at [[Florida State University|Florida State]] for three seasons.<ref name="heatsigning">{{Cite web |date=2007-08-24 |title=Former Grizzlies forward Johnson signs with Heat |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2989937 |access-date=2024-12-02 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> A tough, athletic inside player with a {{convert|40|in|mm|adj=on}} [[vertical leap]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/2006/draft/players/34153.html |title=Sports Illustrated 2006 Draft profile |access-date=2009-10-07 |archive-date=2012-11-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104113301/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/nba/2006/draft/players/34153.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> he averaged 13.2 points, 7.4 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s and 1.0 [[Blocked shot|block]] per game for the [[Florida State University Seminoles|Seminoles]] during the 2005–06 season, his last.

==NBA career==
Johnson was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] 45th overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]], after declaring for the draft in his junior season. His draft rights were traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and subsequently the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on draft day. He played in 59 games during the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]] for the Grizzlies, averaging 4.4 points and 3.1 rebounds per game.<ref name=heatsigning/>

On August 24, 2007, Johnson signed with the [[Miami Heat]]<ref name=heatsigning/> and appeared in 43 games (six starts) for Miami during [[2007–08 NBA season|the campaign]], averaging 4.2 points and 2.2 rebounds, in 12.8 minutes per game.

On June 23, 2008, the Miami Heat announced that they had requested waivers on Johnson. Two months later, he signed with [[Brose Baskets]] of [[Bamberg]], [[Germany]].<ref>[https://thehoop.blogspot.com/2008/09/alexander-johnson-to-brose-baskets.html Alexander Johnson to Brose Baskets]; The Hoop, 14 September 2008</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120729113400/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/35017/448|title=Bamberg completes roster with Alexander Johnson}}; EuroCup Basketball, 15 September 2008</ref>

Johnson later played for the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=alexander_johnson Alexander Johnson D-League profile].</ref>

==CBA career==
In 2012, he signed with the [[Liaoning Hengye Jaguars]] of China.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.niubball.com/teams/ |title=Niubball.com - Teams |access-date=2012-11-23 |archive-date=2013-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203154411/http://www.niubball.com/teams/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the team's second game of the [[2012–13 CBA season]], Johnson tallied a [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] by scoring 23 points and grabbing 11 rebounds.<ref name="Johnson_Tallies_Double_Double">[http://cba.sports.163.com/schedule/report_2012017.html#CNAV2012017ZB] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121203050059/http://cba.sports.163.com/schedule/report_2012017.html#CNAV2012017ZB |date=2012-12-03 }}. Retrieved: December 1st, 2012.</ref> He continued his form by tallying another double-double (21 points, 10 rebounds) in a road loss to the [[Shandong Lions]].<ref name="Shandong_Maintains_Streak">{{cite web|url=http://cba.sports.163.com/schedule/report_2012040.html |title=Archived item |accessdate=2012-12-06 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121209024848/http://cba.sports.163.com/schedule/report_2012040.html |archivedate=2012-12-09 }}, Shandong maintains win streak. Retrieved: December 6th, 2012.</ref>
